findings.measured: Overall L/R correlation is -0.78; likely a polarity problem.

steps.text: The whole mix is out of polarity between left and right. Check the master and bus inserts, and the output routing, for a flip on one side.
Add Utility to the track and turn on Invert for the Left or Right channel only.

findings.measured: Below 150 Hz the correlation is -0.78; bass and kick may thin out in mono.

steps.text: Add Utility to the track (or the Main track) and turn on Bass Mono at about 120 Hz.

other_options.text: Check the kick and bass tracks for chorus, wideners or stereo patches.

findings.measured: The mix loses 9.6 dB when summed to mono.

steps.text: Add Utility to the Main track and switch on Mono.
Lower Utility's Width on the tracks that vanish in mono.
Solo tracks between 0:00 and 0:40 to find the source. Usual suspects: stereo wideners, a very short delay on one side, a stereo bass patch, or double-miked sources.
Add Utility to the track and turn on Invert for the Left or Right channel only.

other_options.text: Watch a correlation meter while you loop 0:00–0:40; it should stay above 0.
Add Utility to the track and turn on Invert for both channels.

notes.headline: One side of your mix is polarity-flipped — L/R correlation is -0.78 for the whole 0:40, and that's behind almost everything else flagged here.
notes.summary: This reads like a straight polarity problem rather than four separate issues: overall correlation is -0.78, it stays negative across the entire 0:00–0:40 (min -0.8), below 150 Hz it's -0.777, and the mix loses 9.6 dB when summed to mono. Fix the flip first and the low-end and mono numbers should largely follow. Levels are otherwise in good shape for a mix going to mastering — true peak -1.41 dBTP and -14.17 LUFS integrated leave plenty of room, so don't chase loudness here.

priorities.title: Polarity flip between left and right
priorities.why: At -0.78 correlation across the whole track, anything that sums to mono — club systems, phone speakers, many streaming/broadcast paths — will cancel rather than add. This is the root cause to chase before touching anything else.

priorities.title: Bass and overall level collapse in mono
priorities.why: Low-end correlation of -0.78 below 150 Hz means kick and bass thin out in mono, and the mix as a whole drops 9.6 dB summed. Re-measure after the polarity fix; if it persists, these steps clean up the remainder.

listen_for: Loop 0:00–0:40 with a correlation meter up — it should sit above 0 rather than near -0.8 (F4.3).
Switch the Main to mono and check the kick and bass still hit with the same weight; that 9.6 dB drop should be gone.
A/B stereo vs mono on a phone or single speaker — the mix shouldn't lose body or center image.
Solo any stereo widener, short one-sided delay or stereo bass patch and confirm it isn't reintroducing the phase issue.
strengths: True peak at -1.41 dBTP leaves safe headroom for mastering.
Peak-to-loudness of 12.8 dB and 5.61 LU loudness range mean you haven't squashed the dynamics.
Left/right balance is dead center at -0.01 dB.

judge.priority_order: Notes correctly place the critical polarity/phase group (F1,F4) before the mono-loss group (F2,F3), matching severity order and treating polarity as root cause of the shared -0.78 correlation values.
judge.explains_impact: Both priorities describe listener-facing consequences: 'anything that sums to mono...will cancel' and 'kick and bass thin out in mono... drops 9.6 dB summed,' not just raw numbers.
judge.groups_causes: F1/F4 (both negative-correlation/polarity findings) and F2/F3 (both mono-collapse findings) are sensibly grouped by shared underlying cause rather than left as four separate items.
judge.specific: Notes cite exact figures (-0.78, -0.777, 9.6 dB, -1.41 dBTP, -14.17 LUFS) and the 0:00–0:40 section, clearly tied to this bounce.
judge.stage_appropriate: Notes explicitly say 'don't chase loudness here' and frame peak/LUFS as headroom for mastering, matching the mix stage in the report.
judge.faithful: Claims (polarity cause, mono cancellation, thin bass, headroom) all trace to reported measurements and findings without inventing unsupported issues; causal link between findings is presented as inference ('reads like') not fact.
judge.concise: Despite covering four findings plus strengths and listen-for cues, each sentence carries specific data or action with no repetition or hype.
